theory.intro: A rounded measurement has limited precision. The absolute error used here is the maximum possible rounding error: half the precision. The limits of accuracy give the corresponding range of possible true values.
facts: The **precision** is the smallest measurement increment used. For an instrument, identify its smallest marked division.
When no different accuracy is stated, use the smallest place value shown: $34$ s has precision $1$ s and $6.3$ kg has precision $0.1$ kg.
A stated accuracy overrides the place value: $180$ m measured to the nearest $10$ m has precision $10$ m.
$\text{Absolute error} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times \text{precision}$. This gives the maximum possible rounding error, rather than the actual difference from an unknown true value.
steps: Identify the precision from the smallest marked division, the stated rounding accuracy or the smallest place value shown.
Calculate $\text{absolute error} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times \text{precision}$, keeping the measurement's units.
If limits of accuracy are requested, subtract the absolute error for the lower bound and add it for the upper bound.

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the precision and maximum absolute error in each case.
(a) $18$ kg
(b) $18.4$ kg
(c) $50$ mL, measured to the nearest $10$ mL.
(d) A ruler has $10$ equal divisions between its $2$ cm and $3$ cm marks. Give the precision and absolute error in centimetres.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Precision $=1$ kg.
(b) Precision $=0.1$ kg.
(c) The stated accuracy gives precision $=10$ mL.
(d) The $1$ cm interval has $10$ equal divisions.
Precision $=\dfrac{3-2}{10}=0.1$ cm.
(a) Absolute error $=\tfrac{1}{2}\times1=0.5$ kg.
(b) Absolute error $=\tfrac{1}{2}\times0.1=0.05$ kg.
(c) Absolute error $=\tfrac{1}{2}\times10=5$ mL.
(d) Absolute error $=\tfrac{1}{2}\times0.1=0.05$ cm.

workedExamples.question_text: A volume is recorded as $4.38$ L, rounded to the nearest $0.01$ L. Find its precision, maximum absolute error and limits of accuracy. Use the usual rounding convention that halfway values round up.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Precision $=0.01$ L.
Absolute error $=\tfrac{1}{2}\times0.01=0.005$ L.
Lower bound $=4.38-0.005=4.375$ L.
Upper bound $=4.38+0.005=4.385$ L.
The true volume $V$ satisfies $4.375\leq V<4.385$, with $V$ in litres.

workedExamples.question_text:
Three rounded measurements of a parcel's mass are $12$ kg, $12.3$ kg and $12.34$ kg. Each is rounded to its smallest displayed place value, with halfway values rounded up.
(a) Find each precision and maximum absolute error, and identify the most precise recorded measurement.
(b) Could all three readings describe the same mass? Use their limits of accuracy to explain.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) For $12$ kg, precision $=1$ kg.
For $12.3$ kg, precision $=0.1$ kg.
For $12.34$ kg, precision $=0.01$ kg.
The reading $12.34$ kg is most precise because its measurement increment is smallest.
For $12$ kg, absolute error $=\tfrac{1}{2}\times1=0.5$ kg.
For $12.3$ kg, absolute error $=\tfrac{1}{2}\times0.1=0.05$ kg.
For $12.34$ kg, absolute error $=\tfrac{1}{2}\times0.01=0.005$ kg.
(b) For $12$ kg, lower bound $=12-0.5=11.5$ kg.
Upper bound $=12+0.5=12.5$ kg.
For $12.3$ kg, lower bound $=12.3-0.05=12.25$ kg.
Upper bound $=12.3+0.05=12.35$ kg.
For $12.34$ kg, lower bound $=12.34-0.005=12.335$ kg.
Upper bound $=12.34+0.005=12.345$ kg.
The intervals are $11.5\leq m<12.5$, $12.25\leq m<12.35$ and $12.335\leq m<12.345$, with $m$ in kilograms.
Their common interval is $12.335\leq m<12.345$.
Yes, all three readings can describe the same mass because their limits overlap.

workedExamples.question_text: The limits of accuracy of a rounded length are $8.65\leq L<8.75$, with $L$ in centimetres. Find the recorded measurement, its maximum absolute error and its precision.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The recorded measurement is the midpoint of the bounds.
Recorded measurement $=\dfrac{8.65+8.75}{2}=8.7$ cm.
The absolute error is the distance from the recorded measurement to either bound.
Absolute error $=8.7-8.65=0.05$ cm.
The precision is twice the absolute error.
Precision $=2\times0.05=0.1$ cm.

A pencil's length is recorded as $27$ cm.

foundation.solution_text:

$\text{Precision} = 1$ cm

development.question_text:
A desk's width is measured as $58$ cm.
Find the limits of accuracy of this measurement.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Precision} = 1$ cm
$\text{Absolute error} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 1$
$= 0.5$ cm
$\text{Lower bound} = 58 - 0.5 = 57.5$ cm
$\text{Upper bound} = 58 + 0.5 = 58.5$ cm
$57.5 \text{ cm} \leq \text{true width} < 58.5 \text{ cm}$

development.question_text: A sprint is timed as $12.7$ s. Find the limits of accuracy of this measurement.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Precision} = 0.1$ s
$\text{Absolute error} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 0.1$
$= 0.05$ s
$\text{Lower bound} = 12.7 - 0.05 = 12.65$ s
$\text{Upper bound} = 12.7 + 0.05 = 12.75$ s
$12.65 \text{ s} \leq \text{true time} < 12.75 \text{ s}$

development.question_text: A bolt's length is measured as $0.83$ m. Between which two values must its true length lie?
development.solution_text:
$\text{Precision} = 0.01$ m
$\text{Absolute error} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 0.01$
$= 0.005$ m
$\text{Lower bound} = 0.83 - 0.005 = 0.825$ m
$\text{Upper bound} = 0.83 + 0.005 = 0.835$ m
$0.825 \text{ m} \leq \text{true length} < 0.835 \text{ m}$

development.question_text: The length $x$ of a wharf is given as $260$ m, to the nearest $10$ m. Write the error interval for $x$.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Precision} = 10$ m
$\text{Absolute error} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 10$
$= 5$ m
$\text{Lower bound} = 260 - 5 = 255$ m
$\text{Upper bound} = 260 + 5 = 265$ m
$255 \text{ m} \leq x < 265 \text{ m}$

development.question_text:
A parcel is weighed as $78.0$ g, correct to one decimal place.
Find the limits of accuracy of this measurement.
development.solution_text:
The trailing zero shows the measurement is to the nearest $0.1$ g.
$\text{Precision} = 0.1$ g
$\text{Absolute error} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 0.1$
$= 0.05$ g
$\text{Lower bound} = 78.0 - 0.05 = 77.95$ g
$\text{Upper bound} = 78.0 + 0.05 = 78.05$ g
$77.95 \text{ g} \leq \text{true mass} < 78.05 \text{ g}$

development.question_text:
A crate is weighed as $435$ kg, to the nearest $5$ kg.
Find the limits of accuracy of this measurement.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Precision} = 5$ kg
$\text{Absolute error} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 5$
$= 2.5$ kg
$\text{Lower bound} = 435 - 2.5 = 432.5$ kg
$\text{Upper bound} = 435 + 2.5 = 437.5$ kg
$432.5 \text{ kg} \leq \text{true mass} < 437.5 \text{ kg}$

development.question_text:
A hike takes $3\tfrac{1}{2}$ hours, to the nearest $\tfrac{1}{2}$ hour.
Find the lower and upper bounds of the true time.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Precision} = 0.5$ h
$\text{Absolute error} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 0.5$
$= 0.25$ h
$\text{Lower bound} = 3.5 - 0.25 = 3.25$ h
$\text{Upper bound} = 3.5 + 0.25 = 3.75$ h
$3.25 \text{ h} \leq \text{true time} < 3.75 \text{ h}$

mastery.question_text:
Priya, Marcus and Elena each measure the mass of the same pumpkin correctly.
Priya records $8$ kg, Marcus records $7.9$ kg and Elena records $7.85$ kg.
Explain how all three can be correct, and state the precision of each person's scale.
mastery.solution_text:
Each scale has a different precision, so each reading is rounded to a different smallest unit.
Priya: precision $1$ kg
Marcus: precision $0.1$ kg
Elena: precision $0.01$ kg
Each reading's limits of accuracy contain the true mass, so all three measurements are correct.

mastery.question_text:
The length $\ell$ of a table satisfies the error interval $45.5 \text{ cm} \leq \ell < 46.5 \text{ cm}$.
What measurement was recorded, and what was the precision of the instrument?
mastery.solution_text:
The recorded measurement is the centre of the interval.
$\dfrac{45.5 + 46.5}{2} = 46$ cm
$\text{Absolute error} = 46 - 45.5 = 0.5$ cm
$\text{Precision} = 2 \times 0.5 = 1$ cm
The recorded measurement was $46$ cm, to the nearest centimetre.

mastery.question_text:
One surveyor records a driveway as $120$ m, to the nearest $10$ m. Another records it as $118$ m, to the nearest metre.
Which measurement is more precise, and what are its limits of accuracy?
mastery.solution_text:
For the $120$ m reading:
$\text{Precision} = 10$ m
$\text{Absolute error} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 10 = 5$ m
For the $118$ m reading:
$\text{Precision} = 1$ m
$\text{Absolute error} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 1 = 0.5$ m
$1 \text{ m} < 10 \text{ m}$, so the $118$ m reading is more precise.
$\text{Lower bound} = 118 - 0.5 = 117.5$ m
$\text{Upper bound} = 118 + 0.5 = 118.5$ m
$117.5 \text{ m} \leq \text{true length} < 118.5 \text{ m}$
